rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The imperative either follows the contrast as its practical consequence, or concludes the preceding argument; in both readings it stands independently.
rows.anchor: جملة { ادفع بالتي هي أحسن } مفصولة غير معطوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was commanded to complete human moral excellence; ʿĀʾisha described his character as the Qurʾan.
rows.anchor: وإنما أمر الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم بذلك لأن منتهى الكمال البشري خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Excellence is intrinsically good, but for legal limits such as punishment foregoing it can be praiseworthy; pursue it unless a greater excellence is at risk.
rows.anchor: والكمال مطلوب لذاته فلا يعدل عنه ما استطاع ما لم يخش فوات كمال أعظم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha reports that the Prophet never avenged himself, except when God's inviolable limits were violated, then he acted for God.
rows.anchor: ما انتقم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لنفسه قط إلا أن تنتهك حرمات الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The community is encouraged to this disposition, linked to the promise that whoever pardons and makes amends has reward with God.
rows.anchor: وجزاء سيئة سيئة مثلها فمن عفا وأصلح فأجره على الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report through ʿIyāḍ, Ibn Mardawayh, Jābir, and Ibn Jarīr says that, after 7:199, Gabriel conveyed God's command to maintain kinship, give to the deprived, and pardon the wrongdoer.
rows.anchor: وروى عياض في ( الشفاء ) وهو مما رواه ابن مردويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted object of “repel” is the evil deed, supplied by the contrast: repel evil with the best deed, as in parallel verses.
rows.anchor: فلما أمر بأن تكون الحسنة مدفوعا بها تعين أن المدفوع هو السيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That which is best” means a good deed; its superlative form encourages responding well because anger naturally inclines people to retaliate.
rows.anchor: وإنما صيغت بصيغة التفضيل ترغيبا في دفع السيئة بها لأن ذلك يشق على النفس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is described as never answering evil with evil, but pardoning and overlooking; this was reportedly his description in the Torah.
rows.anchor: وقد ورد في صفة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sudden-result clause explains the benefit of the command: kindness can bring an enemy close to friendship and thus confirms the command's wisdom.
rows.anchor: وفرع على هذا الأمر قوله : { فإذا الذي بينك وبينه عداوة كأنه ولي حميم }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prefixed “if/when” is suddenative, expressing the rapid appearance of kindness's effect in turning an enemy into a friend.
rows.anchor: وهي كناية عن سرعة ظهور أثر الدفع بالتي هي أحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The relative “one between you” permits an indefinite kind of enmity and a range of strength and duration; the rhetoric implies stronger kindness is needed against more entrenched hostility.
rows.anchor: وهذا تركيب من أعلى طرف البلاغة لأنه يجمع أحوال العداوات فيعلم أن الإحسان ناجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison means hostility has receded and affection has entered; the closeness varies and ordinarily does not reach full intimate friendship.
rows.anchor: وجه الشبه هو المصافاة والمقاربة وهو معنى متفاوت الأحوال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The enmity addressed is religious hostility from polytheism, so the verse does not describe hostility removed by conversion; ʿUmar and Hind illustrate that separate change.
rows.anchor: والعداوة التي بين المشركين وبين النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عداوة في الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muqātil says the verse was revealed about Abū Sufyān, once the Prophet's enemy and later a loyal friend after conversion.
rows.anchor: وعن مقاتل : أنه قال : هذه الآية نزلت في أبي سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr accepts that Abū Sufyān later became friendly but doubts the verse was revealed about him, since it concerns winning affection through kindness.
rows.anchor: فلا أحسب أن الآية نزلت في ذلك لأنها نزلت في اكتساب المودة بالإحسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Walī means ally or supporter, opposite an enemy; ḥamīm means close relative or friend, combining two qualities incompatible with enmity.
rows.anchor: والولي : اسم مشتق من الولاية بفتح الواو ، والولاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next clause is either coordinated with the command or circumstantial to “that which is best”; its pronoun denotes the best conduct in repelling, since good deeds generally can occur without patience.
rows.anchor: وضمير { يلقاهآ } عائد إلى ( التي هي أحسن )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse urges training in this virtue: it takes resolve and patience to restrain the desire for revenge; patience itself is praised and greatly rewarded.
rows.anchor: وهذا تحريض على الارتياض بهذه الخصلة بإظهار احتياجها إلى قوة عزم وشدة مراس للصبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patient people endure hardship and control anger, making it easier for them to forgo retaliation; the verse links to the exception in 103:2–3.
rows.anchor: فالصابر مرتاض بتحمل المكاره وتجرع الشدائد وكظم الغيظ فيهون عليه ترك الانتقام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yulaqqāhā means making oneself attain it, metaphorically likening cultivation of the virtue to seeking and meeting someone; compare 76:11.
rows.anchor: وهو مستعار للسعي لتحصيلها لأن التحصيل على الشيء بعد المعالجة والتخلق يشبه السعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two present-tense verbs portray future cultivation, while past “those who were patient” marks patience as an established prior trait; this explains avoiding “the patient.”
rows.anchor: للدلالة على أن الصبر خلق سابق فيهم هو العون على معاملة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥaẓẓ is a share, sometimes specifically of good; here it is a great share of virtue, right guidance, and piety. Patience is necessary but is only part of the broader qualification.
rows.anchor: والحظ : النصيب من الشيء مطلقا ، وقيل : خاص بالنصيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “none receives it” rather than coordinating the second clause heightens emphasis, leaving no part of the statement subordinate to a conjunction.
rows.anchor: وفي إعادة فعل { وما يلقاها } دون اكتفاء بحرف العطف إظهار لمزيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction “possessor of a great share” presents goodness as a settled disposition; the counsel is not an easy command for everyone.
rows.anchor: وأفاد { ذو حظ عظيم } أن الحظ العظيم من الخير سجيته وملكته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns to an obstacle to gracious conduct: satanic prompting to retaliate should be met by seeking God's protection, which God promises to grant; the address is to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فإن ذلك نزغ من الشيطان دواؤه أن تستعيذ بالله منه فقد ضمن الله له أن يعيذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeking refuge renews the Prophet's innate protection and clears the soul of approaching cloudiness; the Prophet said he sought forgiveness a hundred times daily.
rows.anchor: إنه ليغان على قلبي وإني لأستغفر الله في اليوم مائة مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sacred report in al-Tirmidhī promises that God will grant refuge to the servant who seeks it after drawing near through voluntary acts.
rows.anchor: ولئن استعاذني لأعيذنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that Satan prompts evil and denies truth, while an angel prompts good and confirms truth; one finding the former should seek God's protection.
rows.anchor: حديث ابن مسعود عند الترمذي قال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( إن للشيطان لمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting “the heaven” before its governing verb heightens attention to reflection on its creation.
rows.anchor: وتقديم السماء على الفعل الناصب له زيادة في الاهتمام بالاعتبار بخلقها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mīzān literally names a weighing instrument and by metaphor names justice; here it is the justice God instituted to order creation, as in 57:25.
rows.anchor: والميزان هنا مراد به العدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Waḍʿ, “placing,” metaphorically means appointing justice; after “raising” heaven it forms antithetical wordplay and echoes God's appointing the balance with scripture.
rows.anchor: فالوضع هنا مستعار للجعل فهو كالإنزال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ṭalḥa uses waḍʿ to mean assigning or designating his beloved property, supporting the sense of appointing a purpose.
rows.anchor: أي اجعلها وعينها لما يدلك الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Associating justice with heaven dignifies it as belonging to the realm of truth and virtue and as a divine command sent to earth; the pairing recalls justice in creation and the maxim that heaven and earth stand by justice.
rows.anchor: قرن ذلك مع رفع السماء تنويها بشأن العدل بأن نسب إلى العالم العلوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An can be explanatory because instituting the balance implies commanding justice; then lā is prohibitive and the clause explains avoidance of injustice.
rows.anchor: يجوز أن تكون تفسيرية لأن فعل وضع الميزان فيه معنى أمر الناس بالعدل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively an is a subjunctive particle with an omitted preceding lām, meaning “lest you transgress”; on this parsing lā is negative and taṭghaw is subjunctive.
rows.anchor: مصدرية بتقدير لام الجر محذوفة قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either parsing, the balance means both justice and weighing devices, so divine justice entails avoiding overreach in marketplace measures.
rows.anchor: وعلى كلا الاحتمالين يراد بالميزان ما يشمل العدل ويشمل ما به تقدير الأشياء الموزونة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word mīzān and the surrounding verbs, prepositions, and qist jointly support both senses; their converging double meanings are a feature of Qur'anic inimitability.
rows.anchor: كل هذه تظاهرت على إفادة هذه المعاني وهذا من إعجاز القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ṭughyān in justice is deliberate rejection of right and contempt for its holders; with weights it means short measure.
rows.anchor: والطغيان : دحض الحق عمدا واحتقارا لأصحابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metaphorical ظرفية of “in the balance” forbids even the slightest transgression involving it, not merely destroying the whole balance; 4:5 and a verse by Sabra illustrate partial use of something.
rows.anchor: و { في } من قوله : { في الميزان } ظرفية مجازية تفيد النهي عن أقل طغيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Establish the weight justly” coordinates with the prohibition if that clause is explanatory, or with “He set the balance” if it gives the rationale.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى : { وأقيموا الوزن بالقسط } عطف على جملة { ألا تطغوا في الميزان }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iqāma means making something stand, a metaphor for performing it in the fullest intended manner, as with establishing prayer.
rows.anchor: والإقامة : جعل الشيء قائما ، وهو تمثيل للإتيان به على أكمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Weight in its concrete sense balances objects by heaviness, but here includes measuring quantities, volumes, and other measures.
rows.anchor: والوزن حقيقته : تحقيق تعادل الأجسام في الثقل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qist means justice; Ibn ʿĀshūr says it is a shortened Arabic form of the Roman-derived qistās, also found in the fuller form.
rows.anchor: والقسط : العدل وهو معرب من الرومية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ can mark accompaniment, making justice a constant condition of conduct, or causation, requiring justice as the criterion of measurement; compare 6:152 and 5:8.
rows.anchor: والباء للمصاحبة . والمعنى : اجعلوا العدل ملازما لما تقومونه من أموركم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because pagan merchants practiced short measure, the verse calls it out; “do not diminish the balance” forbids neglecting justice or cheating by weight, depending on the word's sense.
rows.anchor: وقد كان المشركون يعهدون إلى التطفيف في الوزن كما جاء في قوله تعالى : { ويل للمطففين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sentence may coordinate with “What is the Reality?” The second interrogative “what” conveys that people cannot comprehend the Reality's true nature because an extraordinary event is difficult to imagine.
rows.anchor: والاستفهام بها مكنى به عن تعذر إحاطة علم الناس بكنه الحاقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The addressee of “what made you know” is indefinite: the Reality is so great that its true nature is beyond your grasp.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : الحاقة أمر عظيم لا تدركون كنهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What made you know” is a fixed idiom built from interrogative mā and causative adrā, whose verb takes three objects; the first object's underlying role shifts under causation, while the second is suspended by the interrogative.
rows.anchor: وتركيب ( ما أدراك كذا ) مما جرى مجرى المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first mā magnifies by a rhetorical association between asking about extraordinary things and their greatness; it may instead be a question denying anyone knowledge, but both readings create awe.
rows.anchor: و { ما } الأولى استفهامية مستعملة في التهويل والتعظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third mā suspends adrā from governing its two objects, and the masculine singular address is generic rather than directed to one person.
rows.anchor: وكاف الخطاب فيه خطاب لغير معين فلذلك لا يقترن بضمير تثنية أو جمع أو تأنيث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna, and Yaḥyā ibn Sallām say every “what made you know” is later explained, unlike “what makes you know”; if sound, the former promises an outcome while the latter denies knowledge.
rows.anchor: روي عن ابن عباس : كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib observes that Qur'anic “what made you know” formulas are followed by an explanation; Ibn ʿĀshūr takes this as clarifying the report from Ibn ʿAbbās and others.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : كل موضع ذكر في القرآن { وما أدراك } فقد عقب ببيانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀshūr says grammarians have not adequately explained this construction, and some omit it altogether.
rows.anchor: ولم أر من اللغويين من وفى هذا التركيب حقه من البيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the opening question ends at 69:3, the next verse begins an admonition: Thamūd and ʿĀd were destroyed for denying resurrection and recompense, warning Meccans of the same fate.
rows.anchor: وهو تذكير بما حل بثمود وعاد لتكذيبهم بالبعث والجزاء تعريضا بالمشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, if the clauses connect, Thamūd and ʿĀd denied the Resurrection; “the Striker” is a synonym for the Reality, brought forward instead of a pronoun to explain its terrifying force.
rows.anchor: فعدل إلى إظهار اسم ( القارعة ) لأن ( القارعة ) مرادفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thamūd and ʿĀd are named first because Meccan pagans knew them as famous Arab peoples whose lands lay to the north and south.
rows.anchor: لأنهما من الأمم العربية ولأن ديارهما مجاورة شمالا وجنوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following al-Zamakhsharī, Ibn ʿĀshūr prefers treating amshāj as a singular with a plural-like form, directly modifying nutfa; he thinks Sibawayh does not explicitly forbid this and notes Zamakhsharī's close adherence to him.
rows.anchor: والوجه ما ذهب إليه صاحب ( الكشاف ) : أن { أمشاج } مفرد

rows.speaker: الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد
rows.claim: They treat amshāj as a plural; the singular semen is described by the varied properties of its components, each contributing to body parts, intensifying the description as strongly mixed.
rows.anchor: وإذا كان جمعا كما جرى عليه كلام الفراء وابن السكيت والمبرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mixed components include chemical, vegetal, or earthy elements and elements of vital force.
rows.anchor: وهذه الأمشاج منها ما هو أجزاء كيمائية نباتية أو ترابية ومنها ما هو عناصر قوى الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Testing him” is a prospective circumstantial clause: testing means later obligation after rational maturity; it is moved forward for emphasis, although it logically follows guidance.
rows.anchor: وجملة { نبتليه } في موضع الحال من الإنسان وهي حال مقدرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance clause explains testing and is arranged with stylistic variation; obligation reveals how people respond to a great charge.
rows.anchor: وحقيقة الابتلاء : الاختبار لتعرف حال الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human hearing and sight are foundational to thinking and judgment; the intensive forms reflect humans' greater perception and discrimination than animals'.
rows.anchor: ولذلك جاء وصفه بالسميع البصير بصيغة المبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing receives religious law and prophetic calls, while sight examines proofs of God's existence and artistry.
rows.anchor: فبالسمع يتلقى الشرائع ودعوة الرسل وبالبصر ينظر في أدلة وجود الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being made subject to religious duties and law distinguishes humanity, grounds civilization, and leads into the statement that God guided the way.
rows.anchor: وهذا تخلص إلى ما ميز الله به الإنسان من جعله تجاه التكليف واتباع الشرائع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The guidance clause independently explains testing and elaborates the creation of hearing and sight, then turns from them to warning for disbelief and promise for gratitude.
rows.anchor: استئناف بياني لبيان ما نشأ عن جملة { نبتليه }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guiding the way is an extended representation: God is guide, humanity the traveler, religious deeds the path, and success the destination.
rows.anchor: فالله تعالى كالهادي ، والإنسان يشبه السائر المتحير في الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʾabbaṭa Sharran’s couplet shows that the nouns after both immā remain genitive through annexation and that the dual nūn is omitted.
rows.anchor: فإن الاسمين بعد ( إما ) في الموضعين من البيت مجروران بالإضافة ولذلك حذفت النون

rows.speaker: المرزوقي
rows.claim: Al-Marzūqī explains the nominative reading as omitting the nūn because the phrase is lengthy, as though isār lengthened khuṭṭatā.
rows.anchor: وزاد فقال ( وحذف النون إذا رفعت ( إسار ) استطالة للاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both “either” phrases are circumstantial predicates of the pronoun for the human; the two states accompany guidance after its delivery and reflection.
rows.anchor: و { إما شاكرا وإما كفورا } حالان من ضمير الغيبة في { هديناه }

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most grammarians treat immā as a simple particle of specification that neither governs the following noun nor blocks the preceding governor.
rows.anchor: و { إما } حرف تفصيل ، وهو حرف بسيط عند الجمهور

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh analyzes immā as the conditional in plus negative mā, both stripped of their original functions to form a particle of specification.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه : هو مركب من حرف ( إن ) الشرطية و ( ما ) النافية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians call the second immā a coordinator, but Ibn ʿĀshūr calls this arbitrary: the two immās are alike and waw is the actual coordinator, as poetry illustrates.
rows.anchor: وقدّر بعض النحاة { إما } الثانية حرف عطف وهو تحكم

rows.speaker: ابن جني
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī explains the genitive reading of “isār” in Taʾabbaṭa Sharran's couplet as deletion of the dual nun for annexation, since immā does not block annexation; the verse likewise omits the nun.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني : ( أما من جر ( إسار ) فإنه حذف النون للإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person follows one of the two states after receiving and considering guidance: gratitude accepts it; ingratitude turns away, as a traveler could ignore directions and enter danger.
rows.anchor: فإن أخذ بالهدى كان شاكرا وإن أعرض كان كفورا كمن لم يأخذ بإرشاد من يهديه الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse moves on to the recompense of the grateful and ungrateful, beginning with the unbelievers because their mention is nearer; emphatic warning signals a threat without leniency.
rows.anchor: وأكد الخبر عن الوعيد بحرف التأكيد لإدخال الروع عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿtadnā means “prepared”; lexicographers differ whether it derives from doubled dāl or tāʾ-dāl, with Ibn ʿĀshūr favoring separate forms from two dialects and noting distinct usage for war provisions.
rows.anchor: والأظهر أنهما فعلان نشآ من لغتين غير أن الاستعمال خص الفعل ذا التاء بعدة الحرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Chains are iron links used to restrain criminals and captives; collars are large iron rings hung around the neck and attached to chains as the condemned are led to Hell.
rows.anchor: والأغلال : جمع غل بضم الغين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saʿīr means fire made intensely burning by fuel; the passive-derived adjective became a name for Hell.
rows.anchor: والسعير : النار المسعرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The written muṣḥaf has alif after the second lām in salāsil, but readings diverge; several readers tanwīn it in connection and pause on it like a tanwīn accusative.
rows.anchor: بألف بعد اللام الثانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanwīn is normally unexpected for a broken plural in the diptote pattern, but poetic pairing with aghlālan and saʿīran motivates it; prophetic rhyming expressions show the same pairing.
rows.anchor: تعين أن قراءته بالتنوين لمراعاة مزاوجته مع الاسمين اللذين بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Iktālū ʿalā al-nās means they bought measured goods from people; the measured object is omitted because the verb makes it understood.
rows.anchor: فمعنى : { اكتالوا على الناس } اشتروا من الناس ما يباع بالكيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In kālūhum and wazanūhum the sellers are subjects and “them” refers to customers; the construction omits the prepositional lām from kālū lahum and wazanū lahum.
rows.anchor: فالواوان من { كالوهم أو وزنوهم } عائدان إلى اسم الموصول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since kāla and wazana normally take a measured object, omitting the lām is a frequent lightening of “measure/weigh for them,” like common verbs such as thanking someone.
rows.anchor: ولكثرة دورانه على اللسان خففوه فقالوا : كاله ووزنه طعاما

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ says the people of the Ḥijāz and nearby Qays say “measure for us” as well as “measure for them”; others use the direct-object construction only.
rows.anchor: قال الفراء : هو من كلام أهل الحجاز ومن جاورهم من قيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The buyers' side mentions measuring alone because they usually bought produce by measure and paid in weighed coin; sellers use both measure and weight, revealing that the cheating was merchants' practice.
rows.anchor: فلذلك اقتصر في ابتياعهم من الجالبين على الاكتيال نظرا إلى الغالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastawfūn answers “when”: istīfāʾ means taking the full amount, with the added letters intensifying the action.
rows.anchor: والاستيفاء أخذ الشيء وافيا ، فالسين والتاء فيه للمبالغة في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yukhsirūn means they cause their customers to incur a monetary loss by shorting a transaction.
rows.anchor: ومعنى { يخسرون } يوقعون الذين كالوا لهم أو وزنوا لهم في الخسارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage warns Muslims against widespread short-measure practices in early Medina and condemns the polytheists of Medina and Mecca.
rows.anchor: وهذه الآية تحذير للمسلمين من التساهل في التطفيف إذ وجوده فاشيا في المدينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Short measure combines injustice, theft, and meanness, traits the Arabs disdained separately yet practiced together.
rows.anchor: أن التطفيف يجمع ظلما واختلاسا ولؤما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The astonished question about resurrection supports taking the initial warning to address Muslims; sincere Muslims stopped cheating, whereas hypocrites did not.
rows.anchor: يرجح أن الخطاب في قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ẓann means its usual sense: a preponderant belief that the event will occur, as in 45:32.
rows.anchor: والظن : مستعمل في معناه الحقيقي المشهور وهو اعتقاد وقوع الشيء اعتقادا راجحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demonstrative “those” singles the cheaters out for public blame and makes their described trait a reason for the rebuke.
rows.anchor: لقصد تمييزهم وتشهير ذكرهم في مقام الذم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li in “for a tremendous day” marks a time; it also answers a presumed objection that earlier generations were not resurrected by indicating a set time for the event.
rows.anchor: واللام في قوله : { ليوم عظيم } لام التوقيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes the exception disconnected from the pronoun in “give them glad tidings”: the glad tidings to the damned are sarcastic, while “except” introduces a contrasting group.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو استثناء منقطع من ضمير { فبشرهم } فهو داخل في التبشير المستعمل في التهكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected exception's illa functions like “but”; defining istidrāk as removing an assumed implication is only an approximate definition.
rows.anchor: فحرف { إلا } بمنزلة ( لكن ) والاستدراك فيه لمجرد المضادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of an unblemished reward answers how the believers fare; a generous reward carries honor and no reproach, since reminding recipients of a favor spoils it.
rows.anchor: والأجر غير الممنون هو الذي يعطاه صاحبه مع كرامة بحيث لا يعرض له بمنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Nābigha's verse describes one blessing after another as free of the sting of reproach; al-Zamakhsharī says blessings taste sweeter than reminders of favors.
rows.anchor: علي لعمرو نعمة بعد نعمة لوالده ليست بذات عقارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ghayr mamnūn means uninterrupted, from the verb for cutting a rope, as in the description of fruit in 56:32–33.
rows.anchor: غير مقطوع يقال : مننت الحبل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās tells Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq that ghayr mamnūn means uncut; he cites al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza's use of manīn for dust left behind after a fast-moving rider.
rows.anchor: سأل نافع بن الأزرق الخارجي عبد الله بن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath's answer is that humanity is intensely ungrateful to its Lord; kanūd varies by dialect: ingrate among Mudar and Rabīʿa, miser among Kināna, disobedient among Kinda and Ḥaḍramawt.
rows.anchor: والكنود : وصف من أمثلة المبالغة من كند

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generic definite “human” often implies all humanity: self-preference innately inclines people to ingratitude, though prophets and the most complete righteous escape it through self-monitoring and recognition of others' rights.
rows.anchor: وهذا عارض يعرض لكل إنسان على تفاوتت فيه ولا يسلم منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The following clauses explain this innate, variable ingratitude and show that it appears through speech, intention, conduct, or neglect.
rows.anchor: بالقول والقصد ، أو بالفعل والغفلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rāḍiya (content) is a transferred description of life: its possessor is content with it, or the life causes contentment.
rows.anchor: ووصف الحياة ب { راضية } مجاز عقلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “His mother is an abyss” announces misery; it may literally use “mother” as a figurative equivalent of an person's condition, since Arabs associate a person's good or bad fortune with the mother's joy or grief.
rows.anchor: والكلام تمثيل لحال من خفت موازينه يومئذ بحال الهالك في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The formula resembles “his mother perished” or “his mother bereaved him,” an inherited curse also used for wonder; Ibn ʿĀshūr analyzes a cited elegy as ellipsis and semantic abstraction.
rows.anchor: ويقولون في الشر : هوت أمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, umm may be a metaphor for a person's place of refuge and destination, and hāwiya is a deadly low place between mountains, here identified with Hell or as its proper name.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون ( أمه ) مستعارا لمقره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The oath by time confirms the statement, as Qur'anic oaths do, and its object is a sign of God's wondrous creation, power, and knowledge.
rows.anchor: أقسم الله تعالى بالعصر قسما يراد به تأكيد الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Time” has several possible referents; whichever is intended, its significance comes from being a period that manifests divine action, by contextual indication, addition, or shared reference.
rows.anchor: وللعصر معانن يتعين أن يكون المراد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Its common sense is the late afternoon, from when a body's shadow equals its noon shadow to twice that amount, through yellowing sunlight before evening; the poem by al-Ḥārith ibn Ḥilliza uses ʿaṣran for that late time.
rows.anchor: وأشهر إطلاق لفظ العصر أنه علم بالغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afternoon reminds one of the solar-earth system and recurring day-night cycle, the end of daily work and social rhythms, household life, blessings, and the approach of death after life's stages.
rows.anchor: وفيه إيماء إلى التذكير بمثل الحياة حين تدنو آجال الناس بعد مضي أطوار الشباب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception completes the division into those who lose and those untouched by loss; believers who do good avoid loss if they leave no good undone by committing its opposite, or repent.
rows.anchor: فالذين آمنوا وعملوا الصالحات لا يلحقهم الخسران بحال إذا لم يتركوا شيئا من الصالحات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repentance is among the greatest good works; genuine faith with no sin, or sin followed by repentance, yields the opposite of loss: a good final outcome.
rows.anchor: ومن أكبر الأعمال الصالحات التوبة من الذنوب لمقترفيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Loss has degrees: eternal loss comes from denying God's oneness and the Messenger; lesser loss varies with evil deeds, and minor sins may be forgiven when major sins are avoided, as in 11:114.
rows.anchor: فأعظمه وخالده الخسر المنجر عن انتفاء الإيمان بوحدانية الله وصدق الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The loss is in the future life, as the warning context indicates, regardless of worldly fortunes; compare 3:196–197.
rows.anchor: أي لفي خسر في الحياة الأبدية الآخرة فلا التفات إلى أحوال الناس في الحياة الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The indefinite khusr can indicate kinds of loss or intensify and universalize it for dramatic effect.
rows.anchor: وتنكير { خسر } يجوز أن يكون للتنويع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣāliḥāt is generic yet comprehensive of every commanded good deed, including avoiding sins; the exception's relative clause states why they are spared loss.
rows.anchor: والتعريف في قوله : { الصالحات } تعريف الجنس مراد به الاستغراق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Counseling one another about truth includes all religious interests, including Islamic belief and religious ethics; mutual counsel about patience includes good deeds and avoiding sins.
rows.anchor: على إقامة المصالح الدينية كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience underlies the virtues because moral discipline and good deeds require restraining desires; ʿAmr ibn al-ʿĀṣ's verse illustrates the effort.
rows.anchor: فإن الارتياض بالأخلاق الحميدة لا يخلو من حمل المرء نفسه على مخالفة شهوات كثيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A prophetic report says Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires; ʿAlī says patience is a mount that does not stumble.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : ( حفت الجنة بالمكاره وحفت النار بالشهوات )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciprocal form of “counsel one another” makes mutual exhortation to truth and patience a regular feature of believers' lives and presumes they practice what they commend.
rows.anchor: وأفادت صيغة التواصي بالحق وبالصبر أن يكون شأن حياة المؤمنين قائما على شيوع التآمر بهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This presumption recalls God's rebuke to the Children of Israel for enjoining virtue while neglecting it, and the criticism of failing to urge feeding the poor.
rows.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى توبيخا لبني إسرائيل : أتأمرون الناس بالبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word māl can denote camels kept for blood money, orchards among agricultural communities, or cash among Meccans, a trading people; reports about the Anṣār, Abū Ṭalḥa, and al-ʿAbbās illustrate these senses.
rows.anchor: وغلب عند أهل مكة على الدراهم لأن أهل مكة أهل تجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Addadahu means he repeatedly counts it, with the doubled form intensifying his obsessive repetition and love of accumulating wealth.
rows.anchor: فالتضعيف للمبالغة في ( عد ) ومعاودته

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read jamaʿa with an ungeminated mīm; the doubled addadahu then implies repeated counting, which indirectly suggests repeated accumulation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور { جمع مالا } بتخفيف الميم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلف
rows.claim: These readers geminate the mīm in jamaʿa, intensifying accumulation in parallel with the doubled addadahu.
rows.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر ورويس عن يعقوب وخلف بتشديد الميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, addadahu can mean increasing the number or types of wealth, like the enumerated riches of 3:14.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون { عدده } بمعنى أكثر إعداده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The claim that wealth immortalizes its owner may be a sarcastic circumstantial portrait of the hoarder, a detached assertion of denial, or a taunting rhetorical question.
rows.anchor: وجملة : { يحسب أن ماله أخلده } يجوز أن تكون حالا من همزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Past akhlada treats the future as already accomplished because the hoarder is so certain that money has granted immortality, intensifying the satire.
rows.anchor: وجيء بصيغة المضي في { أخلده } لتنزيل المستقبل منزلة الماضي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hamza in akhlada is causative: wealth supposedly makes its possessor immortal.
rows.anchor: والهمزة في { أخلده } للتعدية ، أي جعله خالدا

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce yaḥsabu with kasra on the sīn; Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, Ḥamza, and Abū Jaʿfar use fatḥa, two dialectal forms.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور : { يحسب } بكسر السين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hoarder behaves as if wealth could ward off death and grant the worldly immortality that is his greatest wish, since he denies another eternal life.
rows.anchor: أن المال يقيهم الموت ويجعلهم خالدين لأن الخلود في الدنيا أقصى متمناهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kallā refutes the idea that wealth immortalizes and rebukes obsessive hoarding that prevents paying God's due through spending and zakāt.
rows.anchor: وزجر عن التلبس بالحالة الشنيعة التي جعلتهم في حال من يحسب أن المال يخلد صاحبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An explanatory transition predicts that the mockers will be hurled into al-Ḥuṭama; the pronoun refers to the slanderer and the lām answers an omitted oath.
rows.anchor: والمعنى : ليهلكن فلينبذن في الحطمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nabdh is casting away, commonly of something disliked; al-Zamakhsharī says 28:40 contemptuously likens Pharaoh's people to pebbles thrown from a handful.
rows.anchor: والنبذ : الإلقاء والطرح ، وأكثر استعماله في إلقاء ما يكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥuṭama is an intensive form for something that crushes and breaks; the definite article refers to Hell, and this name for the Fire is Qur'anic rather than an Arab usage.
rows.anchor: والحطمة : صفة بوزن فعلة ، مثل ما تقدم في الهمزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “What made you know al-Ḥuṭama?” is a circumstantial clause whose repeated name instead of a pronoun amplifies terror; the knowledge formula heightens its dread.
rows.anchor: وفعل الدراية يفيد تهويل الحطمة
